'''Magda Galula Ericson '''(born 1929<ref>{{cite web|url=http://viaf.org/viaf/311398419/#Galula-Ericson,_Magda_(1929-_)|title=Galula-Ericson, Magda (1929- )|publisher=VIAF}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Marquis Biographies Online|url = http://search.marquiswhoswho.com/profile/100026875238|website = search.marquiswhoswho.com|access-date = 2015-04-17}}</ref>) is a [[France|French]]-[[Algeria]]n physicist of [[Tunisia]]n origin. Her experimental pioneering PhD work changed the understanding of critical phenomena near the [[Curie temperature|Curie point]]<ref name=":CWP-UCLA" /> and later in her career she has become known for her theoretical development of the [[Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz correction]].

== Contributions ==
Magda Ericson's thesis on the temperature dependence of slow neutron scattering on iron is an important pioneering experimental study of critical phenomena near the [[Curie point]].<ref name=":CWP-UCLA">{{Cite web |date=April 30, 1997 |title=Contributions of 20th century women to physics: Magda Galula Ericson |url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Ericson,_Magda_Galula@881345678.html |access-date=March 8, 2015 |website=CWP at UCLA}}</ref>  Ericson is also known for her theoretical contributions to nuclear [[pion]] physics, which is a subfield of [[nuclear physics]]. She and her husband, [[Torleif Ericson]], discovered the [[Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz correction|Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz]] (EELL) effect of the pion-nuclear [[optical model]], which has implications for electromagnetic and [[weak interactions]] in nuclei.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title = Optical properties of low-energy pions in nuclei|last1 = Ericson|first1 = Magda|date = February 18, 1966|journal = Annals of Physics|volume = 36|issue = 3|pages = 323–362|doi = 10.1016/0003-4916(66)90302-2|last2 = Ericson|first2 = Torleif|bibcode = 1966AnPhy..36..323E|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/346193/files/CM-P00057161.pdf}}</ref><ref name=":CWP-UCLA" /><ref name="Krige III">{{Cite book|last=Krige|first=J.|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gQbgQrYlpIoC&pg=306|title=History of CERN, III|publisher=Elsevier|year=1996|isbn=978-0-08-053403-9|page=306|language=en|chapter=Physics in the CERN Theory Division: CERN, the centre of Europe}}</ref> She is also one of the leading researchers on the interpretation of the [[EMC effect]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=M. |last2=Thomas |first2=A. W. |date=1983-08-18 |title=Pionic corrections and the EMC enhancement of the sea in iron |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=128 |issue=1 |pages=112–116 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)90085-0 |bibcode=1983PhLB..128..112E |issn=0370-2693}}</ref> Magda Ericson's contributions are largely responsible for the development of nuclear pion physics as a subfield of nuclear physics and a large number of papers are based on her work.<ref name=":CWP-UCLA" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Magda Ericson: list of publications sorted by number of citations as recorded by Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=oPpFHuUAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> Ericson continues her research to this day.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Magda Ericson: list of publications indexed by Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=oPpFHuUAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref name="cou">{{cite journal |date=December 2010 |title=Faces and places: CERN lays on birthday treat for the Ericsons |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734476 |journal=CERN Courier |volume=50 |issue=10 |page=41}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Although born in Tunisia, she graduated in 1947 from high-school in [[Algiers]], at that time part of France. Following this she attended preparatory scientific university level classes at Lycée Bugeaud, later called {{Interlanguage link|Lycée Émir-Abdelkader|lt=Lycée Émir-Abdelkader|fr|Lycée Émir-Abdelkader}}, from 1947 to 1949.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1949-07-09 |title=Journal officiel de la République française. Lois et décrets |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k1573313w/f21.image.r=galula |access-date=2022-05-20 |website=Gallica |language=EN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1949-08-01 |title=Journal officiel de la République française. Lois et décrets |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k1573690q |access-date=2022-05-20 |website=Gallica |language=EN}}</ref> Placed first in a national entrance competition, she entered the [[École normale supérieure de Sèvres]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=L'annuaire {{!}} a-Ulm |url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Magda+Ericson |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=www.archicubes.ens.fr}}</ref> In 1953 she placed first in the French national competition for physical sciences (Les agrégés de l'enseignement secondaire).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Les agrégés de l'enseignement secondaire. Répertoire 1809-1960 {{!}} Ressources numériques en histoire de l'éducation |url=http://rhe.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr/?q=agregsecondaire_laureats&nom=Galula&annee_op=%3E&annee%5Bvalue%5D=&annee%5Bmin%5D=&annee%5Bmax%5D=&periode=All&concours=All&items_per_page=10 |access-date=2022-05-13 |website=rhe.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr}}</ref>

From 1953 to 1959 she was research associate (attachée de recherche) of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) at the [[CEA Saclay|Saclay center]] of the [[Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique]], working mainly on slow [[neutron scattering]] and magnetism. She also prepared her PhD  thesis in experimental physics, which she defended at [[Sorbonne University]] in 1958.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=M. |first=Ericson-Galula |date=1958 |title=Étude des fluctuations d'aimantation dans le fer au voisinage de la température de Curie par diffusion des neutrons |trans-title=Study by neutron diffusion of magnetic fluctuations in iron in the Curie temperature region |url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:38073985 |journal=Cea-R-1189 |language=French}}</ref> As stated by [[Jacques Friedel|J. Friedel]]  "''The agreement'' (of the van Hove model<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Van Hove |first=Léon |date=1954-07-01 |title=Correlations in Space and Time and Born Approximation Scattering in Systems of Interacting Particles |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.95.249 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=95 |issue=1 |pages=249–262 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.95.249 |bibcode=1954PhRv...95..249V |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Van Hove |first=Léon |date=1954-09-15 |title=Time-Dependent Correlations between Spins and Neutron Scattering in Ferromagnetic Crystals |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.95.1374 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=95 |issue=6 |pages=1374–1384 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.95.1374 |bibcode=1954PhRv...95.1374V |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>) ''with Ericson's measurements'' ''was good enough for them'' (the later Nobelprize winner [[Pierre-Gilles de Gennes|de Gennes]] and Ericson) ''both to present their theses in quick succession''".<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Brochard-wyart |first1=Francoise |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vt3FCgAAQBAJ |title=P.g. De Gennes' Impact On Science - Volume I: Solid State And Liquid Crystals |last2=Prost |first2=Jacques |last3=Bok |first3=Julien |date=2009-07-29 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4467-75-9 |page=3 |language=en}}</ref> Ericson's pioneering results demonstrate the power of slow neutron scattering for investigating condensed matter.

In spite of these achievements, her temporary position with CNRS was not renewed in 1959. For health reasons she abandoned experiments in favor of theoretical research, first in plasma physics. She received a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright scholarship]] and spent one year at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in the plasma physics group of Sanborn C. Brown. During this period she found the explanation of an unexpectedly observed plasma constriction.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=Magda |last2=Ward |first2=C. Seabury |last3=Brown |first3=Sanborn C. |last4=Buchsbaum |first4=S. J. |year=1962 |title=Containment of Plasmas by High-Frequency Electric Fields |url=http://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1728986 |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |language=en |volume=33 |issue=8 |pages=2429–2434 |doi=10.1063/1.1728986 |bibcode=1962JAP....33.2429E |issn=0021-8979|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Career and later research ==
After her return to France, she obtained a position as a lecturer at the [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules#Lyon|University of Lyon]]. In 1967 she was promoted to professor in the same place, a position she kept until her formal retirement in 1995.<ref name=":CWP-UCLA" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 March 1995 |title=Journal officiel de la Republique française |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000000369522 |access-date=2022-05-20 |website=www.legifrance.gouv.fr}}</ref> She continues her research, and publishes actively, to this day (2022),<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Martini |first1=M. |last2=Ericson |first2=M. |last3=Chanfray |first3=G. |date=2022-07-26 |title=Investigation of the MicroBooNE neutrino cross sections on argon |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevC.106.015503 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en |volume=106 |issue=1 |article-number=015503 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.106.015503 |arxiv=2202.08094 |bibcode=2022PhRvC.106a5503M |s2cid=246866981 |issn=2469-9985}}</ref> as [[professor emeritus]]. Concurrently, her research is pursued at CERN as part-time unpaid visiting scientific associate—a status she has held since 1963.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Seghal |first1=Rashme |title=Discovering the universe, one particle at a time. |url=http://www.rediff.com/news/special/discovering-the-universe-one-particle-at-a-time/20150724.htm |access-date=2015-10-01 |website=Rediff}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=People {{!}} Department of Theoretical Physics |url=https://theory.cern/people |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=theory.cern}}</ref>

Back in Europe, she abandoned a career in experimental physics turning to theoretical physics in the just emerging sub-field in the intersection of nuclear and particle physics, in particular concerning the role of the pion in a nuclear context.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/285021/ |title=1963 International Conference on High-energy Physics and Nuclear Structure: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland 25 Feb - 1 Mar 1963 |date=1963 |publisher=CERN |editor-last=Ericson |editor-first=Torleif Eric Oskar |series=CERN Yellow Reports: Conference Proceedings |location=Geneva}}</ref> This was a fortunate decision since it turned out later that her new field of pion-nuclear physics has various useful analogies to her previous field in condensed matter. A major example is the [[Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz correction|Ericson-Ericson Lorentz-Lorenz]] effect for low energy pions, which she examined in detail with [[Torleif Ericson]] in a basic paper in 1966, an article that over time has been widely cited.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Citation plot for the article as recorded by Inspire-HEP |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/50064 |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> Following the developments of pion low energy theorems, and [[QCD vacuum#Partially conserved axial current|PCAC]] in elementary particle physics, she applied in 1969 these techniques to the pion-nucleus threshold interactions, where the finite size of the nucleus presented a conceptual hurdle.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Ericson |first1=Torleif |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v099AAAAIAAJ |title=Pions and Nuclei |last2=Weise |first2=Wolfram |publisher=Clarendon Press |year=1988 |isbn=978-0-19-852008-5 |pages=369 (see "Notes and further reading", no. 8) |language=en |chapter=Chapter 9: Chiral symmetry and soft pions}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Iliopoulos |first=John |title=Chapter 8 - Physics in the CERN Theory Division |date=1996-01-01 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1874589X9680050X |volume=3 |page=307 |editor-last=Krige |editor-first=John |series=History of CERN |publisher=North-Holland |language=en |doi=10.1016/s1874-589x(96)80050-x |isbn=978-0-444-89655-1 |access-date=2022-11-04|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=M. |last2=Figureau |first2=A. |last3=Molinari |first3=A. |date=1969-05-01 |title=From soft to real pions in nuclei and extended systems |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=501–515 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(69)90037-6 |bibcode=1969NuPhB..10..501E |issn=0550-3213}}</ref> This made her study this phenomenon in a wider perspective. She found that the low energy pion-nuclear equations have a nearly exact counterpart in [[Maxwell's equations|Maxwell equations]] for a polarized medium.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last1=Ericson |first1=Torleif |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v099AAAAIAAJ |title=Pions and Nuclei |last2=Weise |first2=Wolfram |publisher=Clarendon Press |year=1988 |isbn=978-0-19-852008-5 |pages=369 (see "Notes and further reading", no. 9) |language=en |chapter=Chapter 9: Chiral symmetry and soft pions}}</ref> This leads in particular to an understanding of how a basic property of the free neutron [[beta decay]] is modified in the nuclear environment by a pion effect,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ericson |first1=M. |last2=Figureau |first2=A. |last3=Thévenet |first3=C. |date=1973-06-25 |title=Pionic field and renormalization of the axial coupling constant in nuclei |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=19–22 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(73)90242-6 |bibcode=1973PhLB...45...19E |issn=0370-2693}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Delorme |first1=J |last2=Ericson |first2=M |last3=Figureau |first3=A |last4=Thévenet |first4=C |date=1976-11-01 |title=Axial polarizability and weak currents in nuclei |journal=Annals of Physics |language=en |volume=102 |issue=1 |pages=273–322 |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(76)90264-5 |bibcode=1976AnPhy.102..273D |issn=0003-4916}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite book |last1=Ericson |first1=Torleif |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v099AAAAIAAJ |title=Pions and Nuclei |last2=Weise |first2=Wolfram |publisher=Clarendon Press |year=1988 |isbn=978-0-19-852008-5 |pages=401 (see "Notes and further reading", no. 8) |language=en |chapter=Chapter 10: Spin-isospin excitations}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Riska |first=Dan-Olof |date=2003-01-01 |title=Nuclear exchange currents |journal=Nuclear Physics News |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=11–14 |doi=10.1080/10506890308232701 |bibcode=2003NPNew..13...11R |s2cid=119636869 |issn=1061-9127}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ericson |first=Magda |date=2004-04-01 |title=Letter to the Editor |journal=Nuclear Physics News |volume=14 |issue=2 |page=37 |doi=10.1080/10506890491034785 |bibcode=2004NPNew..14...37E |s2cid=220354777 |issn=1061-9127}}</ref> and the explanation of the characteristic quenching effects observed in the low-energy [[Gamow–Teller transitions#Gamow–Teller transition|Gamow–Teller transitions]].<ref name=":4" />

Ericson drew, in the early eighties, attention to the role of pionic physics as one of the origins of the EMC effect.<ref name=":2" />

More recently her research concerns neutrino-nuclear interactions at higher energy, the understanding of which is essential for particle physics research. She has given the explanation of the so-called 'axial anomaly'.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Martini |first1=M. |last2=Ericson |first2=M. |last3=Chanfray |first3=G. |last4=Marteau |first4=J. |date=2010-04-23 |title=Neutrino and antineutrino quasielastic interactions with nuclei |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevC.81.045502 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en |volume=81 |issue=4 |article-number=045502 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.81.045502 |arxiv=1002.4538 |bibcode=2010PhRvC..81d5502M |s2cid=45692898 |issn=0556-2813}}</ref>

Ericson's active career spans over seven decades.<ref name=":1" />

== Private life ==
She is married, since 1957, to Torleif Ericson, a Swedish nuclear physicist who is active at CERN since 1960. Together they have two adult children. The Ericsons reside in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profs. Ericson Torleif and Magda (-Galula) |url=https://www.local.ch/en/d/geneve/1202/prof-ericson-torleif-et-magda-galula-l8_MwE0h13SOJVqlBqwwEg |access-date=2022-05-20 |website=www.local.ch |language=en}}</ref>

Ericson is the aunt of the French mathematician [[Jean-Michel Bismut]]. Her cousin [[David Galula]] was a prominent military theorist.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Marlow|first1=Ann|title=David Galula: His Life and Intellectual Context|date=August 2010|publisher=Strategic Studies Institute|page=21|url=http://www.strategicstudiesinstitute.army.mil/pdffiles/PUB1016.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101105044306/http://www.strategicstudiesinstitute.army.mil/pdffiles/PUB1016.pdf|archive-date=November 5, 2010|access-date=2015-10-01}}</ref>
